3. The tributary sends regular tribute in exchange for {SUZERAIN}'s protection.
4. The tributary keeps military autonomy and does not campaign with the suzerain; the suzerain need not join wars the tributary starts.
5. When attacked, the tributary may request protection; refusal ends the tributary treaty.
6. Wars already affecting the tributary when the treaty is signed are handled by the suzerain under the protection obligation.

3. The garrison kingdom enters {SUZERAIN}'s military system and must campaign with the suzerain and guard the borders, but pays no tribute.\n4. The garrison kingdom may not declare war or handle wars separately from the suzerain.\n5. Refusing defense, attacking the garrison kingdom, or failing to keep it safe will reduce loyalty; when loyalty collapses, it may leave suzerain control.

3. The vassal accepts {SUZERAIN}'s control and owes tribute and military service.\n4. The vassal may not declare war or make peace alone and normally follows the suzerain's wars; the suzerain protects it when attacked.\n5. The vassal's crown is bound by the suzerain; it does not leave automatically under garrison rules unless the suzerain releases it or a new treaty says so.
